description: Playa del Rey sits between the bluffs and the Ballona Wetlands, so homes here face constant marine moisture along with the salt exposure typical of beach-adjacent neighborhoods. Bernardino Martin helps Playa del Rey homeowners keep cooling and heating equipment protected from coastal humidity while maintaining steady comfort in bluff-top homes and lower-lying properties closer to the wetlands.
climate: Mild coastal climate with marine layer, ocean breeze, and salt air exposure

localLife.nature: Playa del Rey sits pinched between the ocean bluffs, the Ballona Wetlands, and the edge of Marina del Rey — the empty Surfridge bluffs just south, once a full neighborhood before LAX cleared it for a runway buffer decades ago, are the clearest physical reminder of how close this enclave sits to the airport.
localLife.community: A small, quiet residential enclave — barely 10,000 people — where the Ballona Wetlands and the marina shape daily life as much as the beach itself, without the density or nightlife of the beach cities just up the coast.
localLife.howWeHelp: We account for the extra humidity that comes off the wetlands in addition to standard ocean salt air, and we keep service visits low-key and unobtrusive in a neighborhood that's genuinely quieter than the beach towns around it.

seasonalNotes.focus: Marine layer and wetlands humidity together make for a damper microclimate than a straight ocean-facing beach town — outdoor equipment here needs a closer eye for moisture-related wear.
Bluff-top homes near the old Surfridge buffer and lower-lying homes near the lagoon age differently — a fall check on either tells us honestly whether coastal humidity has gotten into the ductwork.
